# Establish explicit application-sample admission for concurrent live builtin controls and enable safe bank pairing

Queued/unbriefed retained native outcome of #430 and audit #349 RT-4. No implementation authorization.

The current public HostConsoleHandles exposes independent Send SPSC producer endpoints with untimestamped fader/matrix records. Consumer::try_pop refreshes the producer cursor while draining. Thus records may arrive between the current fader and matrix process calls; browser-exclusive submission/render ownership does not prove native concurrent equivalence.

Deliver an explicit application-sample/epoch admission contract with bounded render cutoff, atomic batch admission, typed backpressure and reliable completion/cancellation semantics, then enable safe native live bank pairing under that earned contract. Before coding, Astra must determine whether admission and pairing require independently closable children and number them. Preserve every existing acknowledged application guarantee; unsupported capabilities require explicit contract decisions, never silent drops/delays. Ask: can an ack precede a drop?

Do not substitute queue emptiness, a length snapshot, arbitrary pop cap, earlier while-pop, or host policy declaration for the missing admission contract. Establish ownership, resource reservation, concurrency/late-record behavior and revision/retirement semantics from current source in a full stateless brief. Keep arithmetic integration off render control work; no allocation, locks, syscalls, unbounded refill-driven draining or shared consumers.

Eventual discriminating gates must drive real concurrent admission/application, distinguish before/after cutoff behavior and queue saturation, prove accepted record loss/cancellation behavior, and compare actual paired versus separate PCM/state plus post-fader observations. No timing authority is granted. #430 serialized bank integration and the scalar successor do not close this retained native outcome or #349 RT-4.

Astra briefs/reviews, Luna1, Sol2/3 then explicit hard-stop rebrief; root owns exact-path checkpoints and synchronized issue/PR delivery with exact-head Astra PASS and required CI.

## Existing mechanisms and their limits

- `builtins-compiler/lib.rs:85–132` defines untimestamped matrix and fader records: matrix/coefficient target or fader/mute target plus smoothing length. `TrackControlProducer` at215 publicly exposes three independent SPSC producers. There is no batch ticket, revision, applied sample or atomic cross-queue commit field. HostConsoleHandles exports these owners; changing its layout/producer behavior is not a free implementation detail.
- `engine/realtime/spsc.rs:418–452` shows is_empty as a cursor observation and try_pop refreshing the producer cursor when its cache empties. A length snapshot or while-pop is not a closed admission epoch. Per-stage queues may refill between old drain points; moving matrix earlier changes which records apply.
- WebEngine `submit_commands` reports its next_absolute_sample only after staged admission; `admit_commands_staged` at1963–2182 validates and counts all destinations before pushing and increments in_flight. Exclusive &mut host ownership prevents concurrent producers during this sequence and render. This is the #442/430 proof, not a native concurrent multi-queue transaction primitive. Reusing its room checks with independently exposed producers would not establish atomic admission.
- `protocol/queue.rs:807–842` validates AutomationBatchSlot before a single fixed batch push and only then adds interval/density/frontier reservations. Its dequeue immediately removes those reservations. The source explicitly identifies cancellation as the only production consumer; there is no render delivery ownership transfer. AutomationRecord carries revision-scoped ParameterHandle and start/end sample/kind/value fields; those are not the console matrix/fader record layout.
- `ProtocolController` at3107 checks batch revision and domains then returns AutomationEnqueued(count/occupancy/capacity/generation). That response certifies admission, not an appliedAtSample promise. `cancel_pending_automation` at3635 reserves reliable-event capacity before dequeue; the current queued-only loop at3655 emits one correctly counted cancellation per batch then resets ordering. It has no notion of already handed-off or partially applied batches.
- Structural commit calls reserved cancellation with RevisionChanged (controller2043); transport locate calls it with TransportLocate (3197). SessionControlProvider keeps a prepared parameter catalog/readback (`host-core/control_provider.rs:192–206,275–323`), not a render consumer. The existing C ABI replacement path already has matched revision/plan-boundary tests; it cannot inherit in-flight cancellation merely by clearing the protocol queue.

Thus current protocol admission is useful precedent and source to extend, but an acked batch copied out through try_dequeue_automation would release overlap/capacity protection before terminal disposition. Current cancellation/revision code would also miss the copied work. That is exactly #140 A's unresolved ownership outcome; implementing it again for #444 creates incompatible cancellation accounting.

## Smallest independently closable prerequisite

Use the already-proposed #140 A outcome, numbered under #140 with #444 as a dependent: **retain accepted reservations through bounded handoff and boundary-acknowledged cancellation**. Keep its scope protocol queue/controller and prepared fixed-capacity service/tests, with production host delivery disabled until an integration child. It earns a usable ownership service, not builtin PCM or either parent closure. No second #444 child should duplicate the same ticket/reservation implementation.

Freeze a configured B-ticket bound, at most B*256 fixed records with checked resource arithmetic, and one reserved terminal-return credit per outstanding ticket. Admission reserves every required resource before exposing a batch. Handoff does not release density/interval/capacity; control releases them only after consuming exactly one valid terminal disposition (or transfers them to equivalent reservations with no gap). Cancellation after handoff requires a render boundary acknowledgement distinguishing applied records from remaining canceled records. Reliable-full refusal leaves ownership and old revision publication intact. The existing queue generation must not be repurposed as a per-render epoch without an explicit new identity definition.

The finite #140 A tests already cover B/B+1, reservation preservation after handoff, overlap/density against in-flight work, terminal credit reuse, duplicate/stale terminal rejection, partial cancellation and generation/reliable-full races. Add no new framework under #444. Root must first adopt/number/approve that exact service; its pending spec cannot be cited as existing infrastructure.

## Separate builtin application integration and finite decisions before coding

Do not silently route existing AutomationEnqueue records into TrackFaderRecord/TrackControlRecord: the former contains parameter values/Point or segment semantics; the latter contains block-target updates including explicit smoothing and a whole matrix. Nor may #140's effect Point sub-slicing imply a builtin segment algorithm. Freeze these three decisions in the future builtin integration brief:

1. **Endpoint and command identity.** Recommended: an additive prepared Rust native builtin admission endpoint retaining the current raw Producer API as Concurrent/separate. It accepts a bounded typed batch of existing fader/mute/matrix targets, explicit requested block application sample and plan revision; it never exposes its internal producer(s). This preserves the old BlockTarget/smoothing arithmetic. Reuse the #140 ownership service if its ticket payload/API can represent these fixed records without changing accepted AutomationEnqueue wire semantics. If the service is intentionally AutomationRecord-specific, freeze a small typed ownership payload adaptation before coding, not conversion through floating parameter handles or a parallel ledger. The exact adaptation remains a decision, not an established source capability.
2. **Acceptance versus application cutoff.** Admission success may promise durable acceptance only, with actual effective sample returned after a render-boundary claim; that matches the existing protocol distinction but requires explicit documentation for this NEW endpoint. An immediate promise of a particular still-open boundary cannot be inferred from a sampled current_sample. Recommended explicit handoff: control publishes a COMPLETE reserved batch into a bounded prepared mailbox; render performs one boundary claim of a closed published slot/epoch, validates its plan generation and freezes that batch population for the call. Work published after that claim remains retained for a later claim, never silently lost. For requested samples already missed at claim, root must choose typed terminal late refusal OR documented applied-next-boundary/counter semantics; do not import #140 D4's effect Point catch-up into BlockTarget behavior by accident. The exact atomic slot state/claim API and its before/after publication race proof must be frozen with the common service. A queue occupancy/length snapshot, emptiness check or loop pop cap is not this protocol.
3. **Lifecycle boundary.** Native plan swap/locate/revision change must reserve cancellation capacity and wait for the matched render claim/cancel acknowledgement before reporting the new lifecycle boundary effective. Old-generation tickets remain owned until that acknowledgement; new plan-local target handles are prepared off render. Provider loss/shutdown retains pending ownership for off-render terminal accounting. Choose the exact existing C ABI/host plan-publication adaptation only after the common ticket API exists. No generation clear may drop acknowledged work, and public raw handles retain their documented lifetime contract.

These are finite endpoint/payload, cutoff/late rule and lifecycle-publication decisions. Do not start Luna on a whole-platform implementation to discover them. An additive native endpoint is recommended over changing the meaning of raw Producer::try_push; root must approve its public contract and whether Rust-only delivery is an acceptable first independently useful host slice before numbering that integration.

The initial integration should apply a claimed batch to BOTH original separate builtin owners before the block's arithmetic, with bounded preallocated routing by prepared plan-local IDs. This earns concurrent admission independently of fusion. Its state visibility must remain identical whether the destination is a bank lane or scalar owner; no duplicate consumers or per-stage independently refilling claim. Only after that delivery contract is qualified may bank pairing and retained scalar pairing consume the same closed-batch view. Separate arithmetic is the authoritative reference for this new endpoint. Existing raw Concurrent plans remain on their old drains; no compatibility claim equates new explicitly timed endpoint behavior with arbitrary legacy concurrent arrival timing.

## Minimum subsequent product proof, retaining bank AND scalar

- Real control and render owners coordinated at deterministic test barriers on either side of the actual publication/claim linearization: complete before-claim batch applies together, after-claim batch stays owned and follows the declared next-boundary/late outcome. No timing-based race test or fake queue-length cutoff.
- Full batch admission/resource/reliable-return saturation leaves all records and reservations intact or rejects the whole batch before ack. Multiple fader/matrix records preserve order and all targets; no ack before partial enqueue/drop. Duplicate completion, cancellation racing claim, revision swap/locate, provider loss and shutdown cannot free or cancel an applied record twice.
- Actual nontrivial PCM/state/readback from separate bank-lane AND actual nonbanked scalar owners at exact first_sample, with asymmetric mute/crossfeed/smoothing. Pending values are not reported applied. Only the supported block-target subset is claimed; arbitrary AutomationEnqueue kinds retain #140's explicit pending/delivery obligations.
- Later pairing children compare paired versus this same admission-enabled separate reference, preserve post-fader send/meter/alias barriers and demonstrate actual selected dispatch. Both native bank and native scalar outcomes remain tracked by #444; neither #430 nor serialized #443 closes them.
- Existing positive allocation/free audit plus repeated render zero of both, bounded ticket/record/destination loops independent of producer refill, exact resource/cap admission and reliable reservation tests. No render controller/model access, allocation, locks, syscalls or terminal event publication.

Canonical semantics remain #140 D5's narrow distinction: existing transient AutomationEnqueue does not edit the canonical base/revision; SessionTransactionApply and stored automation edits still update the same typed model and snapshot transactionally. A new Rust builtin endpoint needs its own explicitly stated live-overlay versus persistent-edit behavior; D5 is not blanket permission to evade canonical session mutations.

Disposition: keep #444 queued. Reuse and number the existing #140 A prerequisite rather than inventing duplicate ownership work. Then brief the bounded native builtin batch delivery endpoint with the three exact decisions above; bank/scalar fusion follows that independently useful admission product. No new issue, code, tests, builds, timing or repository/remote changes were made; only this /tmp brief was written.
